currentContext.expansion: MRPL's FY2025-26 expansion was concentrated in downstream marketing infrastructure and in-refinery debottlenecking/technology upgrades rather than a new refinery train. On the marketing side, the Company commissioned 85 HiQ retail outlets during the year, taking the fully operational network to 252 as on 31 March 2026, and entered Andhra Pradesh with its first outlet there — several further HiQ outlets in Andhra Pradesh are at various stages of construction and commissioning. To support the planned retail expansion it upgraded and modernised depot facilities at Hosur (Tamil Nadu), Hindupur (Andhra Pradesh) and Kasaragod (Kerala), commenced operations at third-party terminals in Mangaluru (Karnataka) and Ennore (Tamil Nadu) under an asset-light model, and expanded polypropylene warehousing in Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. It also signed a deal with ISPRL to lease/rent oil storage capacity of 760 TMT / 5.586 MMBBLs at the ISPRL SPR underground rock cavern at Mangaluru. Inside the refinery, a Phase-II M&I shutdown with catalyst replacement in the CHTU unit was carried out in May-June 2025; CDU-3 column internals were revamped with tray replacement and coalescer installation for better LPG and lean amine distribution; Divided Wall Column technology (licensor M/s DWC Innovations, USA) was implemented and stabilised in the NSU column of CDU-2; and at the Polypropylene Unit commercial production of two new polypropylene grades (65 MFI TWIM and thermoforming) was completed. Energy-conservation schemes — including Aromatic GT power import, RLNG processing in HGU-3, CDU-2 GAPH replacement, DCU debutaniser pressure reduction, insulation upgrades on HP/MP steam lines and HCU-2 APH replacement — delivered total savings of 43,436 MTOE per annum, and integration of power import from the Aromatic Complex enabled shutdown of the refinery's Steam Turbine Generator and utility boilers. Renewable integration was accelerated through green power procurement via MESCOM/GDAM and in-house solar generation. The Innovation Center, recognised by DSIR, is advancing crude-to-chemicals (GOAT technology, commercialised at scale on a modified Petro-FCC), AI/ML optimisers, API intermediates (Isobutyl Benzene, p-Aminophenol, Salicylic Acid) at lab, mini-pilot and demonstration scale, and plastic circularity — with a PET pilot-cum-demo plant funded by OIDB scheduled to be commissioned within FY 2026-27.

risks.risk: Climate change adaptation, resilience and transition
risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity. Key risks are potential operational disruptions from extreme weather events, resource constraints such as water availability, evolving regulatory requirements and significant capital needs associated with energy transition, given the Company's reliance on fossil fuels. Mitigation is through operational resilience measures, regulatory compliance and transition planning, phased investments in energy efficiency and gradual portfolio diversification. Financial implications stated as positive as well as negative.

Non-compliance with GHG emission norms presents legal, financial and reputational risks including exposure to carbon pricing mechanisms, penalties and significant capital requirements for compliance and transition. Rising energy costs and stricter emission standards may also impact operating margins. Addressed through continuous emissions monitoring, energy efficiency initiatives, equipment and process upgrades, best-available technologies and integrating emissions considerations into capital planning.

A material risk given the nature of refinery operations and associated SOx, NOx, particulate matter and VOC emissions. Non-compliance with evolving air quality standards could result in regulatory penalties, operational restrictions or shutdowns, reputational impacts and adverse effects on surrounding communities. Increasingly stringent norms require continuous monitoring, process optimisation and ongoing investment in cleaner fuels and emission-control technologies. Financial implication stated as negative.

Water availability is named as a resource constraint within the climate risk rationale; the BRSR separately identifies water management as an opportunity requiring maximised wastewater recycling, reduced freshwater consumption and advanced water technologies to lower water intensity and strengthen long-term operational resilience.

risks.risk: Board composition non-compliance and dependence on the administrative ministry for director appointments
risks.note: The Company did not meet SEBI requirements for Board composition due to a shortfall in Independent Directors during FY2025-26; after four Independent Directors including the Independent Woman Director completed tenure on 27/03/2026, the Board and all sub-committees — Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders Relationship, Risk Management and CSR — fell short of composition requirements from 28/03/2026 to 31/03/2026. Appointment of directors is handled by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, so remediation is outside the Company's direct control. The Secretarial Auditors made an observation on this.

The entirety of the Company's turnover comes from one activity — crude oil refining and manufacturing of petrochemicals — with High-Speed Diesel and Motor Spirit the dominant products, leaving earnings fully exposed to refining margins and auto-fuel demand with no diversifying business line.

risks.risk: Export dependence and geographic concentration of the marketing footprint
risks.note: A significant share of turnover is exported, exposing the Company to global product cracks and trade disruption, while domestically its institutional dominance and its HiQ retail network are concentrated in Karnataka and adjoining southern states served from a single Mangaluru manufacturing site.

All refining and petrochemicals manufacturing sits at the Mangaluru complex; the planned Phase-II Refinery M&I shutdown with catalyst replacement in the CHTU unit in May-June 2025 illustrates how maintenance or an unplanned outage at one site directly interrupts throughput and dispatch.

thesis: A **blockbuster Q3 driven almost entirely by product cracks**, not crude advantage. EBITDA more than doubled YoY (INR 2,824 cr vs 1,064 cr) as diesel/ATF/MS cracks spiked (HSD ~$15→$21, MS ~$8→$13) amid sanctions-driven market dislocation — more than offsetting the loss of (small, "opportunity") Russian barrels, which MRPL has now fully exited. Best-ever energy efficiency (MBN 67) and fuel-&-loss (10.06%), net debt down to ~INR 9,290 cr (D/E 0.63). Mgmt is candid that the Q3 GRM spike is **not sustainable** — current cracks have already moderated back to ~$14–15 (Q2 levels). The real structural story management is selling is the **pivot from a pure base refinery to a refining-plus-marketing business**: own retail outlets 200 → 250 (FY26-end) → 500 (3yr) → 1,000 (5yr), to capture higher, more stable margins than volatile exports.

**Inventory / one-offs (CALL OUT):** No explicit inventory gain/loss quantified on the call (GRM not published). The EBITDA jump is attributed to **cracks + energy efficiency + optimum throughput**, not inventory — but with GRM withheld, investors cannot isolate inventory or any one-off; treat the headline EBITDA as crack-cycle-driven and explicitly **peaky / not run-rate**.
**Petrochem margin (CALL OUT):** No standalone petrochem (OMPL PP/PX) margin disclosed; sulfur and by-products explicitly treated as "marginal / secondary" items, not strategy.

**9M FY26 colour:** Capex INR 887 cr (of ~1,500 cr FY26 target). Heavy crude ~**70–72%** of slate (9M). Exports ~**40%** of products.
guidance (critical):
- **GRM / cracks:** Will NOT publish GRM. Current cracks ~$14–15 (down from Q3 $21), i.e. **Q2-like trajectory** — Q4 expected "reasonably healthy" but not a Q3 repeat ("very high GRMs market will not sustain").
- **Throughput:** Targeting ~18 MMT annualised run-rate (~120% nameplate); past summer "water blues" (desalination plant) resolved.
- **Petrochem ramp:** IBB (Isobutyl Benzene, pharma intermediate) **pilot** only — commercialisation **3–4 years away**, multiple decision gates; IRR "too early to comment." No near-term petchem earnings.
- **Retail-outlet rollout (KEY):** 200 today → **250 by FY26-end** → **500 in 3 years** → **1,000 in 5 years** (called "conservative/intermediate"). ~120 KL/month/outlet; avg outlet cost ~INR 2 cr (range INR 1.5 cr rural to higher urban). Retail currently only ~**1.5–2%** of volumes/revenue.
- **Capex:** **~INR 1,500 cr/yr** FY26 AND FY27 (similar); INR 887 cr spent in 9M, ramps to ~1,500 cr by Mar; split ~**INR 400–450 cr growth** (retail, grid power, IBB) / rest maintenance & revamp.
- **Marketing infra:** Depots ~INR 50–100 cr each/yr; pipelines ~INR 200 cr (Mumbai, Vizag, Kerala, Bangalore-airport pipeline tender pending); ~INR 500 cr ± near-term marketing infra.
- **Dividend:** Possible — board may consider after a profitable Q4; "on the anvil," subject to capex + debt + payout balance.
- **Bio-ATF:** INR 364 cr plant; CORSIA-compliant blended ATF (1% blend) supply from **2027**.
throughput / pipeline:
- Q3 throughput 4.7 MMT (net) / 4.56 MMT (gross PPAC) — discrepancy = net vs gross crude (revenue driven by net).
- Annualised ~18 MMT, ~120% of 15 MMTPA nameplate; unique 3-separate-crude-train design gives operational/maintenance flexibility (at cost of slightly higher F&L).
- Crude sourcing: ~**40% Middle East** (committed via GoI, led by Saudi Aramco) for stability; balance via tenders + domestic ONGC (East/West coast, Mangala crude) + one-to-one MOUs (TOTSA, ADNOC). **Zero Russian crude** currently (was always "marginal opportunity crude"). **Actively evaluating Venezuelan (heavy/low-API) crude** subject to freight/commercials.
- Heavy-crude bias ~70–72% (9M) — complexity-driven, economics-led (can process down to 15–16 API, e.g. Merey/Maya).
segment (refining / petrochem / marketin:
- **Refining:** Core engine; 15 MMTPA complex refinery, 3 crude trains, ~120% util. Product slate (volume): HSD + ATF ~**50%**, MS ~**15%**, others ~**35%** (incl ~10% fuel & loss).
- **Petrochem:** Legacy OMPL (PP/PX) merged in; not separately quantified on call. New optionality = IBB pilot (pharma intermediate), years from commercialisation. Replacement cost cited ~INR 8,000 cr/MMT pure refining → **>INR 10,000 cr/MMT with petchem**.
- **Marketing/Retail:** Strategic priority. 200 own outlets; superior + more stable margins vs volatile exports. ATF franchise strong via **Shell tie-up** + first-mover CORSIA compliance ("no dent expected in ATF share").
growth / optionality:
- **Retail marketing build-out** (the central thesis): 1,000 outlets in 5yrs is an "intermediate" target; mgmt wants a "full-fledged refining + marketing business," not just refining. Depots/pipelines on East & West coasts (Mumbai, Maharashtra, Vizag, Kerala) + Chennai/Andhra/Telangana marketing offices.
- **ATF / Bio-ATF / CORSIA:** First Indian refinery building Bio-ATF (INR 364 cr); global blended-ATF supply from 2027; Shell JV.
- **Petrochem optionality:** IBB pilot (pharma); legacy PP/PX; longer-dated.
- **Grid-power project:** Cuts F&L below 10% (toward 9.5%) next fiscal — efficiency/cost lever.
- **Bangalore-airport pipeline** (Devangonti–Devanhalli) tender pending — infra optionality.
margins & cost:
- **GRM:** Crack-driven, not absolute-price driven ("we are marked-to-market; margins come from cracks"). Q3 cracks peaked (HSD $21) then normalised to $14–15. GRM no longer published.
- **Crude slate:** ~70–72% heavy (economics-led via complex refinery); ~40% Middle East term; sulfur-treatment facility means high-sulfur crude is "not a deal-breaker."
- **Cost levers:** Grid power (F&L down); LNG via competitive BPCL term contract (low consumption, exploring CGD/parent-ONGC southern gas — "marginal" issue); freight rates spiked in Q3 then "significantly" eased (still above Q1).
- Margin mix shift toward retail = higher, more stable margins vs exports (~40% of products today).
capex:
- **~INR 1,500 cr/yr** (FY26 and FY27, similar). 9M FY26 spend INR 887 cr → ~1,500 cr by Mar (projects reach technical closure).
- Split: ~**INR 400–450 cr growth** (retail outlets, grid power import, IBB, projects) + rest maintenance/revamp.
- Mostly revamp + intermediate-product + minor projects (pipeline rerouting, IBB, grid infra) — NOT a major capacity addition.
- Marketing infra layered on top: depots ~INR 50–100 cr each, pipelines ~INR 200 cr.
capital allocation (deleveraging):
- Net debt **INR 9,290 cr**, D/E 0.63; mgmt prioritises debt reduction but cautiously.
- Debt structure: **NCDs INR 3,260 cr** (next due 2028, locked till then); **ECB $500M (~INR 4,500 cr)** — repayment is a forex trade-off (FX loss if repaid early; awaiting US-trade-deal-driven INR strength).
- Capital allocation framed as 3-way trade-off: own capex vs debt vs dividend.
- Dividend possible after profitable Q4 (board decision).
risks:
- **GRM / crack volatility:** Q3 EBITDA is crack-cycle peak; cracks already down ~30% to $14–15. Earnings highly sensitive to refining-margin cycle; GRM opacity (no disclosure) reduces visibility.
- **Sanctions / crude re-sourcing:** 18th EU sanctions package (effective ~21-Jan) and evolving regime; mgmt "compliant," no Russian crude — but sourcing/freight uncertainty "not going away immediately."
- **Petrochem cycle / execution:** IBB years from commercialisation; legacy PP/PX exposed to petchem down-cycle; no near-term contribution.
- **Leverage / forex:** ~INR 9,300 cr debt; ECB repayment carries forex risk; debt reduction "not very significant" near-term.
- **Valuation / float:** ~88% held by ONGC + HPCL, only ~12% public float (≈1% locked) — a structural overhang on re-rating; PSU OMC valuations depressed on perceived government control of pricing/taxation (e.g. SAED precedent).
- **Freight rates:** Spiked in Q3 (Middle East tensions), eased but still above Q1.
mgmt tone: Confident and notably candid. CFO Devendra Kumar openly acknowledged Q3 cracks/GRM are unsustainable ("market will not be able to sustain"), volunteered the float/valuation problem unprompted ("a question we also ask ourselves"), and was transparent that Russian barrels were always marginal. Promotional on the retail-marketing pivot and ATF/CORSIA leadership. Repeatedly declined to put numbers on GRM, IBB IRR, and exact debt trajectory — guarded on forward specifics while bullish on the structural marketing story. Warm, investor-friendly close (open invitation to visit the refinery).
non-obvious:
- **GRM withheld is the key tell:** with GRM/inventory undisclosed, the headline INR 2,824 cr EBITDA cannot be decomposed — it is implicitly a crack-cycle peak (cracks already back to Q2 levels), so do NOT annualise Q3.
- **Russian-crude exit is a non-event:** mgmt insists product cracks rose far more than the lost Russian discount, so the sanctions hit is net positive for Q3 margins — counter-intuitive vs the usual "loss of cheap crude hurts PSU refiners" narrative.
- **Net vs gross throughput:** the 4.7 vs 4.56 MMT "discrepancy" is just net-vs-gross crude (the ~10% F&L), not an error.
- **Float, not fundamentals, caps the stock:** mgmt explicitly blames ~88% promoter holding (ONGC + HPCL) + perceived government price/tax control for the depressed ~INR 25,000 cr market cap vs ~INR 7,000–10,000 cr/MMT replacement cost on 15 MMTPA — they are examining the low-float issue WITH the parent.
- **Retail is still tiny** (~1.5–2% of volumes) — the marketing thesis is multi-year optionality, not current earnings.
- **IBB / Bio-ATF** are long-dated, sub-scale (pilot / INR 364 cr) — narrative/ESG flavour more than near-term P&L.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- Sanctions-driven crude/product dislocation → refiners with complex slates + product-crack leverage (MRPL itself; other PSU refiners) capturing elevated cracks. ⭐
- PSU OMC low-float / valuation overhang → potential beneficiary is any future ONGC/HPCL stake-dilution or OFS that improves MRPL float (structural re-rating optionality). ✅
- India "refining hub" push (Hardeep Puri narrative) → domestic refining-capex and marketing-infra (depots/pipelines/EPC) suppliers. ✅

thesis: A **blockbuster Q3 driven almost entirely by product cracks**, not crude advantage. EBITDA more than doubled YoY (INR 2,824 cr vs 1,064 cr) as diesel/ATF/MS cracks spiked (HSD ~$15→$21, MS ~$8→$13) amid sanctions-driven market dislocation — more than offsetting the loss of (small, "opportunity") Russian barrels, which MRPL has now fully exited. Best-ever energy efficiency (MBN 67) and fuel-&-loss (10.06%), net debt down to ~INR 9,290 cr (D/E 0.63). Mgmt is candid that the Q3 GRM spike is **not sustainable** — current cracks have already moderated back to ~$14–15 (Q2 levels). The real structural story management is selling is the **pivot from a pure base refinery to a refining-plus-marketing business**: own retail outlets 200 → 250 (FY26-end) → 500 (3yr) → 1,000 (5yr), to capture higher, more stable margins than volatile exports.
scorecard (yoy where available; one-offs:
| Metric | Q3 FY26 | Q3 FY25 (YoY) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **EBITDA** | **INR 2,824 cr** | INR 1,064 cr | **YoY +165%**; driven by product cracks, energy efficiency, throughput |
| **GRM / core margin** | Not disclosed (discontinued from Q2) | — | Indicative: ~**double of Q1 margin**, similar range cumulatively. CALL OUT: company stopped publishing GRM citing lack of standardisation across PSUs |
| **Cracks ($/bbl)** | HSD **$21**, MS **$13**, ATF similar | HSD ~$15, MS ~$8 (Q2 base) | CALL OUT: cracks since moderated to ~**$14–15** ("current published") = back to Q2 trajectory; Q3 had spikes beyond $21 |
| **Throughput** | **4.7 MMT** (net crude) / 4.56 MMT (gross, PPAC) | — | Annualised run-rate ~**18 MMT** (~120% of 15 MMTPA nameplate); F&L gap of ~10% explains net vs gross |
| **Utilisation** | ~120% of nameplate | — | But-for Q1 shutdown, FY run-rate ~18 MMT |
| **Fuel & loss** | **10.06%** | — | Best-ever; grid-power project to cut to **9.5–10%** next fiscal |
| **Net / current debt** | **INR 9,290 cr** (D/E 0.63) | — | Expected to ease further if market stays favourable |
| **MBN (energy index)** | 67 | — | Best-ever any quarter |

**Inventory / one-offs (CALL OUT):** No explicit inventory gain/loss quantified on the call (GRM not published). The EBITDA jump is attributed to **cracks + energy efficiency + optimum throughput**, not inventory — but with GRM withheld, investors cannot isolate inventory or any one-off; treat the headline EBITDA as crack-cycle-driven and explicitly **peaky / not run-rate**.
**Petrochem margin (CALL OUT):** No standalone petrochem (OMPL PP/PX) margin disclosed; sulfur and by-products explicitly treated as "marginal / secondary" items, not strategy.

**9M FY26 colour:** Capex INR 887 cr (of ~1,500 cr FY26 target). Heavy crude ~**70–72%** of slate (9M). Exports ~**40%** of products.
guidance (critical):
- **GRM / cracks:** Will NOT publish GRM. Current cracks ~$14–15 (down from Q3 $21), i.e. **Q2-like trajectory** — Q4 expected "reasonably healthy" but not a Q3 repeat ("very high GRMs market will not sustain").
- **Throughput:** Targeting ~18 MMT annualised run-rate (~120% nameplate); past summer "water blues" (desalination plant) resolved.
- **Petrochem ramp:** IBB (Isobutyl Benzene, pharma intermediate) **pilot** only — commercialisation **3–4 years away**, multiple decision gates; IRR "too early to comment." No near-term petchem earnings.
- **Retail-outlet rollout (KEY):** 200 today → **250 by FY26-end** → **500 in 3 years** → **1,000 in 5 years** (called "conservative/intermediate"). ~120 KL/month/outlet; avg outlet cost ~INR 2 cr (range INR 1.5 cr rural to higher urban). Retail currently only ~**1.5–2%** of volumes/revenue.
- **Capex:** **~INR 1,500 cr/yr** FY26 AND FY27 (similar); INR 887 cr spent in 9M, ramps to ~1,500 cr by Mar; split ~**INR 400–450 cr growth** (retail, grid power, IBB) / rest maintenance & revamp.
- **Marketing infra:** Depots ~INR 50–100 cr each/yr; pipelines ~INR 200 cr (Mumbai, Vizag, Kerala, Bangalore-airport pipeline tender pending); ~INR 500 cr ± near-term marketing infra.
- **Dividend:** Possible — board may consider after a profitable Q4; "on the anvil," subject to capex + debt + payout balance.
- **Bio-ATF:** INR 364 cr plant; CORSIA-compliant blended ATF (1% blend) supply from **2027**.
throughput / pipeline:
- Q3 throughput 4.7 MMT (net) / 4.56 MMT (gross PPAC) — discrepancy = net vs gross crude (revenue driven by net).
- Annualised ~18 MMT, ~120% of 15 MMTPA nameplate; unique 3-separate-crude-train design gives operational/maintenance flexibility (at cost of slightly higher F&L).
- Crude sourcing: ~**40% Middle East** (committed via GoI, led by Saudi Aramco) for stability; balance via tenders + domestic ONGC (East/West coast, Mangala crude) + one-to-one MOUs (TOTSA, ADNOC). **Zero Russian crude** currently (was always "marginal opportunity crude"). **Actively evaluating Venezuelan (heavy/low-API) crude** subject to freight/commercials.
- Heavy-crude bias ~70–72% (9M) — complexity-driven, economics-led (can process down to 15–16 API, e.g. Merey/Maya).
segment (refining / petrochem / marketin:
- **Refining:** Core engine; 15 MMTPA complex refinery, 3 crude trains, ~120% util. Product slate (volume): HSD + ATF ~**50%**, MS ~**15%**, others ~**35%** (incl ~10% fuel & loss).
- **Petrochem:** Legacy OMPL (PP/PX) merged in; not separately quantified on call. New optionality = IBB pilot (pharma intermediate), years from commercialisation. Replacement cost cited ~INR 8,000 cr/MMT pure refining → **>INR 10,000 cr/MMT with petchem**.
- **Marketing/Retail:** Strategic priority. 200 own outlets; superior + more stable margins vs volatile exports. ATF franchise strong via **Shell tie-up** + first-mover CORSIA compliance ("no dent expected in ATF share").
growth / optionality:
- **Retail marketing build-out** (the central thesis): 1,000 outlets in 5yrs is an "intermediate" target; mgmt wants a "full-fledged refining + marketing business," not just refining. Depots/pipelines on East & West coasts (Mumbai, Maharashtra, Vizag, Kerala) + Chennai/Andhra/Telangana marketing offices.
- **ATF / Bio-ATF / CORSIA:** First Indian refinery building Bio-ATF (INR 364 cr); global blended-ATF supply from 2027; Shell JV.
- **Petrochem optionality:** IBB pilot (pharma); legacy PP/PX; longer-dated.
- **Grid-power project:** Cuts F&L below 10% (toward 9.5%) next fiscal — efficiency/cost lever.
- **Bangalore-airport pipeline** (Devangonti–Devanhalli) tender pending — infra optionality.
margins & cost:
- **GRM:** Crack-driven, not absolute-price driven ("we are marked-to-market; margins come from cracks"). Q3 cracks peaked (HSD $21) then normalised to $14–15. GRM no longer published.
- **Crude slate:** ~70–72% heavy (economics-led via complex refinery); ~40% Middle East term; sulfur-treatment facility means high-sulfur crude is "not a deal-breaker."
- **Cost levers:** Grid power (F&L down); LNG via competitive BPCL term contract (low consumption, exploring CGD/parent-ONGC southern gas — "marginal" issue); freight rates spiked in Q3 then "significantly" eased (still above Q1).
- Margin mix shift toward retail = higher, more stable margins vs exports (~40% of products today).
capex:
- **~INR 1,500 cr/yr** (FY26 and FY27, similar). 9M FY26 spend INR 887 cr → ~1,500 cr by Mar (projects reach technical closure).
- Split: ~**INR 400–450 cr growth** (retail outlets, grid power import, IBB, projects) + rest maintenance/revamp.
- Mostly revamp + intermediate-product + minor projects (pipeline rerouting, IBB, grid infra) — NOT a major capacity addition.
- Marketing infra layered on top: depots ~INR 50–100 cr each, pipelines ~INR 200 cr.
capital allocation (deleveraging):
- Net debt **INR 9,290 cr**, D/E 0.63; mgmt prioritises debt reduction but cautiously.
- Debt structure: **NCDs INR 3,260 cr** (next due 2028, locked till then); **ECB $500M (~INR 4,500 cr)** — repayment is a forex trade-off (FX loss if repaid early; awaiting US-trade-deal-driven INR strength).
- Capital allocation framed as 3-way trade-off: own capex vs debt vs dividend.
- Dividend possible after profitable Q4 (board decision).
risks:
- **GRM / crack volatility:** Q3 EBITDA is crack-cycle peak; cracks already down ~30% to $14–15. Earnings highly sensitive to refining-margin cycle; GRM opacity (no disclosure) reduces visibility.
- **Sanctions / crude re-sourcing:** 18th EU sanctions package (effective ~21-Jan) and evolving regime; mgmt "compliant," no Russian crude — but sourcing/freight uncertainty "not going away immediately."
- **Petrochem cycle / execution:** IBB years from commercialisation; legacy PP/PX exposed to petchem down-cycle; no near-term contribution.
- **Leverage / forex:** ~INR 9,300 cr debt; ECB repayment carries forex risk; debt reduction "not very significant" near-term.
- **Valuation / float:** ~88% held by ONGC + HPCL, only ~12% public float (≈1% locked) — a structural overhang on re-rating; PSU OMC valuations depressed on perceived government control of pricing/taxation (e.g. SAED precedent).
- **Freight rates:** Spiked in Q3 (Middle East tensions), eased but still above Q1.
mgmt tone: Confident and notably candid. CFO Devendra Kumar openly acknowledged Q3 cracks/GRM are unsustainable ("market will not be able to sustain"), volunteered the float/valuation problem unprompted ("a question we also ask ourselves"), and was transparent that Russian barrels were always marginal. Promotional on the retail-marketing pivot and ATF/CORSIA leadership. Repeatedly declined to put numbers on GRM, IBB IRR, and exact debt trajectory — guarded on forward specifics while bullish on the structural marketing story. Warm, investor-friendly close (open invitation to visit the refinery).
non-obvious:
- **GRM withheld is the key tell:** with GRM/inventory undisclosed, the headline INR 2,824 cr EBITDA cannot be decomposed — it is implicitly a crack-cycle peak (cracks already back to Q2 levels), so do NOT annualise Q3.
- **Russian-crude exit is a non-event:** mgmt insists product cracks rose far more than the lost Russian discount, so the sanctions hit is net positive for Q3 margins — counter-intuitive vs the usual "loss of cheap crude hurts PSU refiners" narrative.
- **Net vs gross throughput:** the 4.7 vs 4.56 MMT "discrepancy" is just net-vs-gross crude (the ~10% F&L), not an error.
- **Float, not fundamentals, caps the stock:** mgmt explicitly blames ~88% promoter holding (ONGC + HPCL) + perceived government price/tax control for the depressed ~INR 25,000 cr market cap vs ~INR 7,000–10,000 cr/MMT replacement cost on 15 MMTPA — they are examining the low-float issue WITH the parent.
- **Retail is still tiny** (~1.5–2% of volumes) — the marketing thesis is multi-year optionality, not current earnings.
- **IBB / Bio-ATF** are long-dated, sub-scale (pilot / INR 364 cr) — narrative/ESG flavour more than near-term P&L.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- Sanctions-driven crude/product dislocation → refiners with complex slates + product-crack leverage (MRPL itself; other PSU refiners) capturing elevated cracks. ⭐
- PSU OMC low-float / valuation overhang → potential beneficiary is any future ONGC/HPCL stake-dilution or OFS that improves MRPL float (structural re-rating optionality). ✅
- India "refining hub" push (Hardeep Puri narrative) → domestic refining-capex and marketing-infra (depots/pipelines/EPC) suppliers. ✅

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.

hero.oneLiner: Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) is a Schedule "A" Mini Ratna Central Public Sector Enterprise and a subsidiary of ONGC that refines crude oil and manufactures and markets petroleum and petrochemical products from its Mangaluru complex.
